classes.name: HiSparseConfig
classes.doc: Configuration for HiSparse sparse-MLA KV offloading.

fields.name: device_buffer_size
fields.doc: Total per-request GPU hot-buffer rows, including the newest-token slot.

fields.name: eager_host_mirror
fields.doc: Mirror decode-written KV rows to the host pool during the forward so page spills complete without moving data. When disabled, decode rows stay resident-only and evicted pages are copied to host at spill time. Prefill rows are always mirrored during the forward.

classes.name: AttentionConfig
classes.doc: Configuration for attention mechanisms in vLLM.

fields.name: backend
fields.doc: Attention backend to use. Use "auto" or None for automatic selection.

fields.name: minimax_m3_msa_decode_backend
fields.doc: Sparse decode kernel used by the MiniMax M3 MSA backend.

fields.name: backend_per_kind
fields.doc: Per-KV-cache-group attention backend overrides, keyed by `KVCacheSpecKind` (e.g. `{"mla_attention": "FLASHINFER_MLA", "sliding_window_mla": "TRITON_MLA"}`). This lets a model that splits its layers across multiple KV-cache groups (e.g. interleaved full and sliding-window attention) use a different backend per group.

fields.name: flash_attn_version
fields.doc: Force vllm to use a specific flash-attention version (2, 3, or 4). Only valid when using the flash-attention backend.

fields.name: flash_attn_max_num_splits_for_cuda_graph
fields.doc: Flash Attention max number splits for cuda graph decode.

fields.name: tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv
fields.doc: Minimum KV splits for TokenSpeed MLA decode. The default of 1 preserves automatic scheduling. Larger values request a split floor and may increase workspace memory. Only applies to the TokenSpeed MLA backend.

fields.name: tq_max_kv_splits_for_cuda_graph
fields.doc: TurboQuant max NUM_KV_SPLITS for cuda graph decode. Fixes the split count so grid dimensions are constant across captures, and buffers can be pre-allocated to avoid inflating the memory estimate.

fields.name: use_trtllm_attention
fields.doc: If set to True/False, use or don't use the TRTLLM attention backend in flashinfer. If None, auto-detect the attention backend in flashinfer.

fields.name: disable_flashinfer_q_quantization
fields.doc: If set, when using fp8 kv, do not quantize Q to fp8.

fields.name: mla_prefill_backend
fields.doc: MLA prefill backend to use. If None, will be selected automatically. Valid options: FLASH_ATTN (FA3/FA4), FLASHINFER, TRTLLM_RAGGED.

fields.name: use_prefill_query_quantization
fields.doc: If set, quantize query for attention in prefill.

fields.name: trtllm_ragged_backend
fields.doc: Kernel backend for cached-context TRTLLM_RAGGED MLA prefill. CuTe DSL requires FP8 queries for head dimension 192 and does not support head dimension 256. New-token prefill always uses TRTLLM.

fields.name: indexer_kv_dtype
fields.doc: Data type for the sparse-attention indexer K cache. "auto" picks the model's default (bf16 for MiniMax M3, fp8 for the DeepSeek sparse indexer). Quantized formats (fp8, mxfp4, nvfp4) require indexer kernel support in the backend.

fields.name: indexer_sparse_logits
fields.doc: DeepSeek V4.1 two-level indexer: score only the candidate blocks with DeepGEMM's sparse MQA-logits kernels instead of computing dense logits over the whole context and masking them. Requires `indexer_kv_dtype="mxfp4"`, an SM100-class GPU, DeepGEMM >= 2.8 and the DeepSelect top-k extension (the top-k runs on the kernels' bf16 logits). The sparse path costs O(candidate blocks) per query regardless …

fields.name: indexer_tp_shard_min_rows
fields.doc: Minimum total prefill rows for the sparse-attention indexer to split them across TP ranks instead of scoring every row on each rank.

fields.name: minimax_m3_indexer_cp
fields.doc: MiniMax M3 on ROCm with tensor_parallel_size > 1: score the sparse indexer context-parallel at decode. Each rank reads 1/TP of the index cache, scores every index head on it, and per-head top-k candidates are exchanged and merged, so the selected blocks match the default path. Requires a bf16 index cache (`indexer_kv_dtype` "auto" or "bf16").

fields.name: hisparse_config
fields.doc: HiSparse host-resident KV configuration. Setting this enables experimental Model Runner V2-only HiSparse sparse-MLA decode hot-buffering. It is inferred with defaults when HiSparseConnector is configured (directly or via MultiConnector); set it explicitly only to tune its fields.

fields.name: use_non_causal
fields.doc: Whether to use non-causal (bidirectional) attention.

fields.name: sparse_mla_force_mqa
fields.doc: Force sparse MLA to use forward_mqa for all requests, including prefill. When False (default), pure prefill batches use forward_mha when implemented. Set to True to always use the MQA path.

fields.name: sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor
fields.doc: Sparse MLA prefill workspace size, in multiples of `max_model_len`. FlashMLA sparse gathers a prefill step's context KV into this workspace and runs attention in more chunks when the step holds more. The sparse indexer's prefill K buffer is sized to fit in the same memory. Lower values return memory to the KV cache at long `max_model_len`; the minimum of 2 leaves room for a full-length request's …

fields.name: flex_attn_block_m
fields.doc: Triton kernel BLOCK_M tile size for flex attention. Must be a power of 2 >= 16. If None and VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1, defaults to 16.

fields.name: flex_attn_block_n
fields.doc: Triton kernel BLOCK_N tile size for flex attention. Must be a power of 2 >= 16. If None and VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1, defaults to 16.

fields.name: flex_attn_q_block_size
fields.doc: Logical Q block size for the flex attention block mask. Must be a power of 2 and divisible by flex_attn_block_m. If None, uses 16 for paged KV attention on PyTorch >= 2.9, and 128 for encoder-only attention or older PyTorch versions.

fields.name: flex_attn_kv_block_size
fields.doc: Logical KV block size for the flex attention block mask. Must be a power of 2 and divisible by flex_attn_block_n. If None, uses the KV cache block size for paged KV attention on PyTorch >= 2.9, and 128 for encoder-only attention or older PyTorch versions.

classes.doc: Configuration for auxiliary-output delivery.

fields.name: enable_return_routed_experts
fields.doc: Capture and return routed-experts auxiliary outputs.

fields.name: max_bytes
fields.doc: LRU capacity, or ``None`` to derive it from the KV cache capacity.

classes.name: CacheConfig
classes.doc: Configuration for the KV cache.

fields.name: block_size
fields.doc: Size of a contiguous cache block in number of tokens. Accepts None (meaning "use default"). After construction, always int.

fields.name: user_specified_block_size
fields.doc: Whether block_size was explicitly provided. Derived automatically.

fields.name: kv_cache_layout
fields.doc: Resolved physical KV cache layout name (a ``KVCacheLayout`` member).

fields.name: prefix_match_unit
fields.doc: The finest token boundary (in tokens) a prefix-cache hit can land on.

fields.name: gpu_memory_utilization
fields.doc: The fraction of GPU memory to be used for the model executor, which can range from 0 to 1. For example, a value of 0.5 would imply 50% GPU memory utilization. If unspecified, will use the default value of 0.92. This is a per-instance limit, and only applies to the current vLLM instance. It does not matter if you have another vLLM instance running on the same GPU. For example, if you have two vLLM …

fields.name: cache_dtype
fields.doc: Data type for kv cache storage. If "auto", will use model data type. An explicit float16 or bfloat16 must match the model data type. Custom dtypes can registered by platform backends via ``register_kv_cache_dtype`` are accepted (see vllm.config.cache). CUDA 11.8+ supports fp8 (=fp8_e4m3) and fp8_e5m2. ROCm (AMD GPU) supports fp8 (=fp8_e4m3). Intel Gaudi (HPU) supports fp8 (using fp8_inc). Some …

fields.name: is_attention_free
fields.doc: Whether the model is attention-free. This is primarily set in `ModelConfig` and that value should be manually duplicated here.

fields.name: num_gpu_blocks_override
fields.doc: Number of GPU blocks to use. This overrides the profiled `num_gpu_blocks` if specified. Does nothing if `None`. Used for testing preemption.

fields.name: sliding_window
fields.doc: Sliding window size for the KV cache. This is primarily set in `ModelConfig` and that value should be manually duplicated here.

fields.name: enable_prefix_caching
fields.doc: Whether to enable prefix caching.

fields.name: prefix_caching_hash_algo
fields.doc: Set the hash algorithm for prefix caching:

fields.name: prefix_cache_retention_interval
fields.doc: Token interval between retained sliding-window and Mamba prefix-cache checkpoints. ``0`` retains only semantic checkpoints, including the latest replay boundary and shared-prefix junctions. Positive values additionally retain periodic checkpoints at the specified interval, which must be a multiple of the scheduler block size. ``None`` retains checkpoints densely. Applies only to sliding-window …

fields.name: kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers
fields.doc: Layer patterns to skip KV cache quantization. Accepts layer indices (e.g., '0', '2', '4') or attention type names (e.g., 'sliding_window').

fields.name: mamba_page_size_padded
fields.doc: Optional override for mamba page size; used by hybrid mamba/attention models to ensure exact alignment with attention page size.

fields.name: skip_page_size_padded
fields.doc: Optional override for the page size of layers skipped from KV cache quantization (``--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers``); set during block-size alignment so unquantized skip layers pad up to the quantized primary's page.

fields.name: mamba_block_size
fields.doc: Size of a contiguous cache block in number of tokens for mamba cache. Can be set only when prefix caching is enabled.

fields.name: mamba_cache_dtype
fields.doc: The data type to use for the Mamba cache (both the conv as well as the ssm state). If set to 'auto', the data type will be inferred from the model config.

fields.name: mamba_ssm_cache_dtype
fields.doc: The data type to use for the Mamba cache (ssm state only, conv state will still be controlled by mamba_cache_dtype). If set to 'auto', the data type for the ssm state will be determined by mamba_cache_dtype.

fields.name: mamba_cache_mode
fields.doc: The cache strategy for Mamba layers, derived from `enable_prefix_caching`:

fields.name: enable_mamba_shared_prefix_checkpoint
fields.doc: Also register a Mamba "align" checkpoint at the shared-prefix junction -- where an EAGLE/MTP sibling was observed to resume -- instead of only at the prompt tail. Off by default; only takes effect with prefix caching enabled, EAGLE on the Mamba group, and a prefix match unit smaller than the Mamba block size.

fields.name: replayssm_buffer_len
fields.doc: ReplaySSM logical history length B for Mamba2. Triton uses B physical rows and FlashInfer uses B+T, where T is the target verification length. Kimi-K3 speculative decode does not use B. Default 16.

fields.name: use_replayssm
fields.doc: Use the ReplaySSM Mamba2 decode kernel: cache recent SSM inputs and skip the per-step full-state store, writing the checkpoint back only on flush. Requires the Triton or FlashInfer mamba backend; FlashInfer does not support prefix caching yet. Mamba2 speculative decode requires FlashInfer. With prefix caching, flushes are most efficient when mamba_block_size is a multiple of replayssm_buffer_len, …

fields.name: use_kda_recoverssm
fields.doc: Whether Kimi-K3 KDA uses RecoverSSM speculative decode.

fields.name: num_gpu_blocks
fields.doc: The number of blocks to allocate for GPU memory.

fields.name: num_cpu_blocks
fields.doc: The number of blocks to allocate for CPU memory.

fields.name: simple_cpu_offload_num_blocks
fields.doc: Worker-aligned offload block count for ``SimpleCPUOffloadConnector``.

fields.name: effective_attention_block_size
fields.doc: Full-attention block size in tokens, including DCP, or None if unavailable.

fields.name: kv_cache_size_tokens
fields.doc: Per-DP-engine KV cache capacity in tokens (group-aware). Uses group-aware capacity since num_gpu_blocks * block_size can be wrong for hybrid models where requests occupy multiple KV cache groups.

fields.name: kv_cache_max_concurrency
fields.doc: Per-DP-engine maximum concurrency at max_model_len tokens.

fields.name: hash_block_size
fields.doc: Tokens per prefix-cache block hash.

fields.name: cache_hit_alignment_tokens
fields.doc: Token granularity at which prefix-cache hits land: `hash_block_size` with partial hash hits, otherwise the scheduler block size.

fields.name: kv_sharing_fast_prefill
fields.doc: In some KV sharing setups, e.g. YOCO (https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05254), some layers can skip tokens corresponding to prefill. This flag enables attention metadata for eligible layers to be overridden with metadata necessary for implementing this optimization in some models (e.g. Gemma3n)

fields.name: swa_bounded_replay
fields.doc: Keep the sliding-window KV of models that support it (DeepSeek-V4.1) out of prefix caching and rebuild it after a prefix hit by recomputing the hit's last window. The layers past the last KV-source layer then also run eager prefill steps on each request's trailing window only. Requires model runner V2.

fields.name: kv_cache_memory_bytes
fields.doc: Size of KV Cache per GPU in bytes. By default, this is set to None and vllm can automatically infer the kv cache size based on gpu_memory_utilization. However, users may want to manually specify the kv cache memory size. kv_cache_memory_bytes allows more fine-grain control of how much memory gets used when compared with using gpu_memory_utilization. Note that kv_cache_memory_bytes (when not-None) …

fields.name: kv_offloading_size
fields.doc: Size of the KV cache offloading buffer in GiB. When TP > 1, this is the total buffer size summed across all TP ranks. By default, this is set to None, which means no KV offloading is enabled. When set, vLLM will enable KV cache offloading to CPU using the kv_offloading_backend.

fields.name: kv_offloading_backend
fields.doc: The backend to use for KV cache offloading. Supported backends include 'native' (vLLM native CPU offloading), 'lmcache'. KV offloading is only activated when kv_offloading_size is set.

fields.name: _block_size_resolved
fields.doc: Guard against pydantic re-running _apply_block_size_default.

fields.doc: Fuse paired q/kv RMS norms in MLA attention.

fields.doc: Fuse QK RMSNorm + RoPE/MRoPE + KV cache update into an AITER HIP kernel. Supersedes both enable_qk_norm_rope_fusion and fuse_rope_kvcache for layers that support it. Auto-enabled at O2+ on ROCm for models with QK-norm (e.g. Qwen3-MoE and Qwen3-VL-class architectures).

fields.name: rope_kvcache_fusion_max_token_num
fields.doc: The threshold for ROCm AITER RoPE+KVCache fusion e.g. for small batch decode. Larger batch sizes e.g. during prefill will use the unfused kernels. Also applies to the fused QK-Norm+RoPE/MRoPE+KVCache pass.

fields.name: fi_allreduce_fusion_max_size_mb
fields.doc: The threshold of the communicated tensor sizes under which vllm should use flashinfer fused allreduce. Specified as a float in MB. Unspecified will fallback to default values which are compute capability and world size dependent. FI_ALLREDUCE_FUSION_MAX_SIZE_MB = { 90: { 2: 64, # 64MB 4: 2, # 2MB 8: 1, # 1MB }, 100: { 2: 64, # 64MB 4: 32, # 32MB 8: 1, # 1MB }, }, where key is the device capability

And a failure will be triggered if a recompilation ever happens due to that. This mode requires VLLM_USE_BYTECODE_HOOK to be 0. fields.name: debug_dump_path
fields.doc: The path to dump the debug information.

fields.name: cache_dir
fields.doc: The directory to store the compiled graph, to accelerate Inductor compilation. By default, it will use model-related information to generate a cache directory.

fields.name: compile_cache_save_format
fields.doc: Format for saving torch compile cache:

fields.name: backend
fields.doc: The backend for compilation. It needs to be a string:

fields.name: custom_ops
fields.doc: Fine-grained control over which custom ops to enable/disable. Use 'all' to enable all, 'none' to disable all. Also specify a list of custom op names to enable (prefixed with a '+'), or disable (prefixed with a '-'). Examples:

fields.name: ir_enable_torch_wrap
fields.doc: If True, enable vllm_ir torch custom op wrapping during the forward pass. When False, torch custom op wrapping is disabled, allowing Dynamo to trace the selected implementation directly or avoiding torch custom op overhead in eager mode. Defaults to True when using Inductor with vllm-compile (backend=="inductor" and mode == VLLM_COMPILE), False otherwise.

fields.name: splitting_ops
fields.doc: A list of ops to exclude from cudagraphs, used in piecewise compilation.

fields.name: compile_mm_encoder
fields.doc: Whether or not to compile the multimodal encoder. Currently, this only works for `Qwen2_5_vl` and `mLLaMa4` models on selected platforms. It may also work for models loaded with the Transformers modeling backend if the encoder is compilable. Disabled by default until more models are supported/tested to work.

fields.name: cudagraph_mm_encoder
fields.doc: Enable CUDA graph capture for multimodal encoder (ViT). When enabled, captures full encoder forward as CUDA graph for each token budget level.

fields.name: encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets
fields.doc: Token budget levels for encoder CUDA graph capture. Each budget defines a fixed token capacity. At runtime, images are greedy-packed into the smallest fitting budget and the corresponding CUDA graph is replayed. If empty (default), auto-inferred from model architecture as power-of-2 levels from the model's estimated min budget to max budget. User-provided values override auto-inference. Example: …

fields.name: encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch
fields.doc: Maximum number of images/videos per batch for encoder CUDA graph capture. Determines the fixed batch size used during graph capture. If 0 (default), auto-inferred as max_budget // min_budget from the model's budget range. User-provided positive value overrides auto-inference.

fields.name: encoder_cudagraph_max_frames_per_batch
fields.doc: Maximum total video frames per batch for encoder CUDA graph capture. Controls the cu_seqlens buffer size (one entry per attention sequence, i.e. one per video frame). If None (default), auto-inferred as encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch * max_frames_per_video (model-specific value according to processing_info). Positive value overrides auto-inference and applies to all budget levels. …

fields.name: cudagraph_decoder_replay
fields.doc: Run the decoder replay layers of YOCO models (e.g. DeepSeek-V4.1) in CUDA graphs of their own, and trim them in PIECEWISE graph steps. Requires breakable PIECEWISE graphs; off under LoRA, prompt embeddings and non-first PP ranks.

fields.name: decoder_replay_cudagraph_capture_sizes
fields.doc: Decoder replay CUDA graph sizes for YOCO models (e.g. DeepSeek-V4.1), at most max_num_batched_tokens. If empty: multiples of sliding_window up to min(max_cudagraph_capture_size, max_num_seqs * sliding_window), coarser past 16 * sliding_window. Larger replay batches run eagerly.

fields.name: decoder_replay_trim_threshold
fields.doc: For YOCO models (e.g. DeepSeek-V4.1), PIECEWISE graphs with at least this many padded tokens trim the decoder replay batch; must exceed the replay window (128), below which nothing trims. Independent of the replay graph capture sizes; eager steps still trim.

fields.name: compile_sizes
fields.doc: Sizes to compile for inductor. In addition to integers, it also supports "cudagraph_capture_sizes" to specify the sizes for cudagraph capture.

fields.name: compile_ranges_endpoints
fields.doc: Endpoints for Inductor compile ranges. The compile ranges are [1, endpoints[0]], [endpoints[0] + 1, endpoints[1]], ..., [endpoints[-1] + 1, max_num_batched_tokens]. Compile sizes are also used single element ranges, the range is represented as [compile_sizes[i], compile_sizes[i]].

fields.name: inductor_compile_config
fields.doc: Additional configurations for inductor. - None: use default configurations.

fields.name: inductor_passes
fields.doc: Additional passes for inductor. It is a dictionary from pass name to pass function qualified name. We use function name because the config uses JSON format. If we pass the config from Python, functions can also be passed directly via Python object constructor, e.g. `CompilationConfig(inductor_passes={"a": func})`.

fields.name: cudagraph_mode
fields.doc: The mode of the cudagraph:

fields.name: cudagraph_num_of_warmups
fields.doc: Number of warmup runs for cudagraph. It means the first several runs will be treated as warmup runs. Only after that, the execution will be recorded, and the recorded cudagraph will be used for subsequent runs.

fields.name: cudagraph_capture_sizes
fields.doc: Sizes to capture cudagraph. - None (default): capture sizes are inferred from vllm config. - list[int]: capture sizes are specified as given.

fields.name: cudagraph_copy_inputs
fields.doc: Whether to copy input tensors for cudagraph. If the caller can guarantee that the same input buffers are always used, it can set this to False. Otherwise, it should set this to True, and the compiler will copy the input to an internally managed buffer. Default is False. Note that this flag is only effective when cudagraph_mode is PIECEWISE.

fields.name: cudagraph_specialize_lora
fields.doc: Whether to create separate cuda graphs for cases with and without active LoRA adapters. When set to False, the LoRA-enabled cuda graph will be used for all cases, incurring the overhead of running LoRA ops even when no adapters are active. fields.name: use_inductor_graph_partition

It generates a single `call` function which wraps cudagraph-safe ops into partition functions and leave cudagraph-unsafe ops outside the partition functions. fields.name: enable_rocm_segmented_attn_autotune

fields.name: enable_jit_warmup

fields.name: max_queue_size
fields.doc: The maximum number of events to queue while waiting for publishing.

fields.name: topic
fields.doc: The topic to use for the event publisher. Consumers can subscribe to this topic to receive events.

fields.doc: The KV connector for vLLM to transmit KV caches between vLLM instances.

fields.name: model_loader_extra_config

fields.name: device

fields.name: ignore_patterns
fields.doc: The list of patterns to ignore when loading the model. Default to "original/**/*" to avoid repeated loading of llama's checkpoints.

fields.name: use_tqdm_on_load
fields.doc: Whether to enable tqdm for showing progress bar when loading model weights.

fields.doc: The map location for loading pytorch checkpoint, to support loading checkpoints can only be loaded on certain devices like "cuda", this is equivalent to `{"": "cuda"}`. classes.name: LoggingConfig

fields.name: formatter

fields.name: configure_logging

fields.name: pylogging_config_file

classes.name: LoRAConfig
classes.doc: Configuration for LoRA.

fields.name: max_lora_rank
fields.doc: Max LoRA rank.

fields.name: max_loras
fields.doc: Max number of LoRAs in a single batch.

fields.name: fully_sharded_loras
fields.doc: By default, only half of the LoRA computation is sharded with tensor parallelism. Enabling this will use the fully sharded layers. At high sequence length, max rank or tensor parallel size, this is likely faster.

fields.name: max_cpu_loras
fields.doc: Maximum number of LoRAs to store in CPU memory. Must be >= than `max_loras`.

fields.name: lora_dtype
fields.doc: Data type for LoRA. If auto, will default to base model dtype.

fields.name: target_modules
fields.doc: Restrict LoRA to specific module suffixes (e.g., ["o_proj", "qkv_proj"]). If None, all supported LoRA modules are used. This allows deployment-time control over which modules have LoRA applied, useful for performance tuning.

fields.name: default_mm_loras
fields.doc: Dictionary mapping specific modalities to LoRA model paths; this field is only applicable to multimodal models and should be leveraged when a model always expects a LoRA to be active when a given modality is present. Note that currently, if a request provides multiple additional modalities, each of which have their own LoRA, we do NOT apply default_mm_loras because we currently only support one …

fields.name: enable_tower_connector_lora
fields.doc: If `True`, LoRA support for the tower (vision encoder) and connector of multimodal models will be enabled. This is an experimental feature and currently only supports some MM models such as the Qwen VL series. The default is False.

fields.name: specialize_active_lora
fields.doc: Whether to construct lora kernel grid by the number of active LoRA adapters. When set to True, separate cuda graphs will be captured for different counts of active LoRAs (powers of 2 up to max_loras), which can improve performance for variable LoRA usage patterns at the cost of increased startup time and memory usage. Only takes effect when cudagraph_specialize_lora is True.

fields.name: enable_mixed_moe_lora_format
fields.doc: If True, force the engine to use the universal 2D MoE LoRA wrapper (`FusedMoEWithLoRA`) regardless of the model's `is_3d_moe_weight` flag, so that 2D-format and 3D-format MoE LoRA adapters can be served in the same deployment. Only meaningful for MoE models; ignored otherwise. Default False keeps the existing model-driven behavior.

fields.name: enable_moe_shared_loras
fields.doc: If True, load MoE expert adapters in the "shared-outer" layout, where the gate/up (`w1`/`w3`) lora_A and the down (`w2`) lora_B are shared across all experts (stored once with expert-dim 1) instead of per-expert. The shared factors are broadcast to the expert count at kernel time. 3D-weight MoE models use `FusedMoEWithLoRA` for this layout. Only meaningful for MoE models whose adapters use this …

fields.name: max_lora_cls_labels
fields.doc: Maximum output size for LoRA classification heads. Defaults to the base classification head size.

classes.name: MambaConfig
classes.doc: Configuration for Mamba SSM backends.

fields.name: backend
fields.doc: Mamba SSU backend to use.

fields.name: enable_stochastic_rounding
fields.doc: Enable stochastic rounding when writing SSM state to fp16 cache. Uses random bits to unbias the rounding error, which can improve numerical stability for long sequences.

fields.name: stochastic_rounding_philox_rounds
fields.doc: Number of Philox PRNG rounds for stochastic rounding random number generation. 0 uses the Triton default. Higher values improve randomness quality at the cost of compute.

fields.name: ssu_algorithm
fields.doc: Selective state update algorithm to use with the FlashInfer backend. None defaults to FlashInfer's "auto" algorithm. Forced algorithms must be supported by FlashInfer for the active GPU, state dtype, and decoding mode.

classes.name: ModelConfig
classes.doc: Configuration for the model.

fields.name: model
fields.doc: Name or path of the Hugging Face model to use. It is also used as the content for `model_name` tag in metrics output when `served_model_name` is not specified.

fields.name: model_weights
fields.doc: Original model weights path. Used when the model is pulled from object storage (e.g., RunAI) to preserve the original URI while `model` points to the local directory.

fields.name: runner
fields.doc: The type of model runner to use. Each vLLM instance only supports one model runner, even if the same model can be used for multiple types.

fields.name: convert
fields.doc: Convert the model using adapters defined in [vllm.model_executor.models.adapters][]. The most common use case is to adapt a text generation model to be used for pooling tasks.

fields.name: tokenizer
fields.doc: Name or path of the Hugging Face tokenizer to use. If unspecified, model name or path will be used.

fields.name: tokenizer_mode
fields.doc: Tokenizer mode:

fields.name: trust_remote_code
fields.doc: Trust remote code (e.g., from HuggingFace) when downloading the model and tokenizer.

fields.name: dtype
fields.doc: Data type for model weights and activations:

fields.name: seed
fields.doc: Random seed for reproducibility.

fields.name: hf_config
fields.doc: The Hugging Face config of the model.

fields.name: hf_text_config
fields.doc: The Hugging Face config of the text model (same as hf_config for text models).

fields.name: is_submodel_config
fields.doc: Whether this is a submodule view derived by `VllmConfig.with_hf_config` (e.g. a multimodal model's text stack). Its architecture list is empty, so deployment-level validation must not run against it.

fields.name: word_embeddings_untied_by_checkpoint
fields.doc: Whether `tie_word_embeddings` was overridden to `False` because the checkpoint contains an `lm_head` of its own. The two may still turn out to be identical, in which case they are re-tied once the weights have been loaded.

fields.name: hf_config_path
fields.doc: Name or path of the Hugging Face config to use. If unspecified, model name or path will be used.

fields.name: allowed_local_media_path
fields.doc: Allowing API requests to read local images or videos from directories specified by the server file system. This is a security risk. Should only be enabled in trusted environments.

fields.name: allowed_media_domains
fields.doc: If set, only media URLs that belong to this domain can be used for multi-modal inputs.

fields.name: revision
fields.doc: The specific model version to use. It can be a branch name, a tag name, or a commit id. If unspecified, will use the default version.

fields.name: code_revision
fields.doc: The specific revision to use for the model code on the Hugging Face Hub. It can be a branch name, a tag name, or a commit id. If unspecified, will use the default version.

fields.name: tokenizer_revision
fields.doc: The specific revision to use for the tokenizer on the Hugging Face Hub. It can be a branch name, a tag name, or a commit id. If unspecified, will use the default version.

fields.name: max_model_len
fields.doc: Model context length (prompt and output). If unspecified, will be automatically derived from the model config.

fields.name: spec_target_max_model_len
fields.doc: Specify the maximum length for spec decoding draft models.

fields.name: quantization
fields.doc: Method used to quantize the weights. If `None`, we first check the `quantization_config` attribute in the model config file. If that is `None`, we assume the model weights are not quantized and use `dtype` to determine the data type of the weights.

fields.name: quantization_config
fields.doc: User-facing quantization configuration. Carries per-layer-kind specs (linear, moe) and ignore patterns; see :class:`QuantizationConfigArgs`. Auto-populated from the matching online shorthand when `quantization` is one of the values in `ONLINE_QUANT_SHORTHAND_NAMES`.

fields.name: allow_deprecated_quantization
fields.doc: Whether to allow deprecated quantization methods.

fields.name: enforce_eager
fields.doc: Whether to always use eager-mode PyTorch. If True, we will disable CUDA graph and always execute the model in eager mode. If False, we will use CUDA graph and eager execution in hybrid for maximal performance and flexibility.

fields.name: return_sampling_mask
fields.doc: Whether to return the post-processing token support for each sample.

fields.name: max_logprobs
fields.doc: Maximum number of log probabilities to return when `logprobs` is specified in `SamplingParams`. The default value comes the default for the OpenAI Chat Completions API. -1 means no cap, i.e. all (output_length * vocab_size) logprobs are allowed to be returned and it may cause OOM.

fields.name: logprobs_mode
fields.doc: Indicates the content returned in the logprobs and prompt_logprobs. Supported mode: 1) raw_logprobs, 2) processed_logprobs, 3) raw_logits, 4) processed_logits. Raw means the values before applying any logit processors, like bad words. Processed means the values after applying all processors, including temperature and top_k/top_p. Note: for prompt_logprobs, processed_* and raw_* yield identical …

fields.name: use_fp64_gumbel
fields.doc: Whether to use FP64 (instead of FP32) random noise for Gumbel-max and equivalent exponential-race sampling. FP64 preserves lower-tail sampling events that fp32 uniform/exponential draws can truncate, at the cost of significantly lower throughput on most GPUs.

fields.name: enable_trace_replay
fields.doc: Whether to allow requests to set `SamplingParams.trace_decode_token_ids`, which forces decoding to follow a predetermined token sequence while still computing real logprobs. Reserved for debugging and RL workflows: enabling it reserves a per-request trace buffer, so it is off by default.

fields.name: disable_sliding_window
fields.doc: Whether to disable sliding window. If True, we will disable the sliding window functionality of the model, capping to sliding window size. If the model does not support sliding window, this argument is ignored.

fields.name: disable_cascade_attn
fields.doc: Deprecated: cascade attention has been removed, so this has no effect. It will be removed in v0.33.0.

fields.name: skip_tokenizer_init
fields.doc: Skip initialization of tokenizer and detokenizer. Expects valid `prompt_token_ids` and `None` for prompt from the input. The generated output will contain token ids.

fields.name: enable_prompt_embeds
fields.doc: If `True`, enables passing text embeddings as inputs via the `prompt_embeds` key.

fields.name: served_model_name
fields.doc: The model name(s) used in the API. If multiple names are provided, the server will respond to any of the provided names. The model name in the model field of a response will be the first name in this list. If not specified, the model name will be the same as the `--model` argument. Noted that this name(s) will also be used in `model_name` tag content of prometheus metrics, if multiple names …

fields.name: config_format
fields.doc: The format of the model config to load:

fields.name: hf_token
fields.doc: The token to use as HTTP bearer authorization for remote files . If `True`, will use the token generated when running `hf auth login` (stored in `~/.cache/huggingface/token`).

fields.name: hf_overrides
fields.doc: If a dictionary, contains arguments to be forwarded to the Hugging Face config. If a callable, it is called to update the HuggingFace config.

fields.name: model_class_overrides
fields.doc: Override the model class used for one or more architectures, mapping the architecture name to a `"module:class"` target (the same format accepted by `ModelRegistry.register_model`). This registers the target class at runtime, e.g. `{"GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM": "vllm.models.deepseek_v32.nvidia.model:DeepseekV32ForCausalLM"}`. This argument is for development and debugging purposes only.

fields.name: generation_config
fields.doc: The folder path to the generation config. Defaults to `"auto"`, the generation config will be loaded from model path. If set to `"vllm"`, no generation config is loaded, vLLM defaults will be used. If set to a folder path, the generation config will be loaded from the specified folder path. If `max_new_tokens` is specified in generation config, then it sets a server-wide limit on the number of …

fields.name: override_generation_config
fields.doc: Overrides or sets generation config. e.g. `{"temperature": 0.5}`. If used with `--generation-config auto`, the override parameters will be merged with the default config from the model. If used with `--generation-config vllm`, only the override parameters are used.

fields.name: enable_sleep_mode
fields.doc: Enable sleep mode for the engine (only cuda and hip platforms are supported).

fields.name: sleep_preserve_parameter_names
fields.doc: Parameter-name globs to preserve across level-2 sleep. Use target globs for frozen Engram table weights and scales omitted by the trainer (e.g. ``*.engram.embed_tokens.weight*``). Use ``draft.<name>`` for draft-private parameters, or ``draft.*`` for all. The sender must omit these parameters; loaders must preserve their storage.

fields.name: sleep_mode_backend
fields.doc: Mechanism used to free and restore GPU state for sleep mode. ``"cumem"`` (default) uses the built-in ``CuMemAllocator`` and is behavior-compatible with prior releases. Additional backends (CUDA checkpoint, CRIU, durable snapshot) may be registered in-tree or by plugins (RFC #34303).

fields.name: sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph
fields.doc: Back up CUDA graph memory to CPU during sleep, restored in place on wake. Takes effect with enable_sleep_mode, the cumem backend and CUDA graphs.

fields.name: enable_nccl_comm_suspend
fields.doc: Enable releasing NCCL communicator memory during sleep mode (``ncclCommSuspend``/``ncclCommResume``). Experimental; when disabled (the default) sleep still releases weights/KV-cache memory as before.

fields.name: enable_cumem_allocator
fields.doc: Enable the custom cumem allocator to leverage advanced GPU memory allocation features such as multi-node NVLink support.

fields.name: model_impl
fields.doc: Which implementation of the model to use:

fields.name: logits_processors
fields.doc: One or more logits processors' fully-qualified class names or class definitions

fields.name: io_processor_plugin
fields.doc: IOProcessor plugin name to load at model startup

fields.name: renderer_num_workers
fields.doc: Number of worker threads in the renderer thread pool. The pool is consumed by the async renderer path (e.g. the OpenAI-compatible API server started by `vllm serve`) to parallelize tokenization, chat template rendering, and multimodal preprocessing across concurrent requests.

fields.name: pooler_config
fields.doc: Pooler config which controls the behaviour of output pooling in pooling models.

fields.name: multimodal_config
fields.doc: Configuration for multimodal model. If `None`, this will be inferred from the architecture of `self.model`.

classes.name: MultiModalConfig
classes.doc: Controls the behavior of multimodal models.

fields.name: language_model_only
fields.doc: If True, disables all multimodal inputs by setting all modality limits to 0. Equivalent to setting `--limit-mm-per-prompt` to 0 for every modality.

fields.name: limit_per_prompt
fields.doc: The maximum number of input items and options allowed per prompt for each modality.

fields.name: enable_mm_embeds
fields.doc: If `True`, enables passing multimodal embeddings: for `LLM` class, this refers to tensor inputs under `multi_modal_data`; for the OpenAI-compatible server, this refers to chat messages with content `"type": "*_embeds"`.

fields.name: media_io_kwargs
fields.doc: Additional args passed to process media inputs, keyed by modalities. For example, to set num_frames for video, set `--media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"num_frames": 40} }'`

fields.name: mm_processor_kwargs
fields.doc: Arguments to be forwarded to the model's processor for multi-modal data, e.g., image processor. Overrides for the multi-modal processor obtained from `transformers.AutoProcessor.from_pretrained`.

fields.name: mm_device_do_normalize
fields.doc: Move the do_normalize computation in the mm preprocessing to before the ViT, and let the device do it, so that CPU computation can be saved.

fields.name: mm_processor_cache_gb
fields.doc: The size (in GiB) of the multi-modal processor cache, which is used to avoid re-processing past multi-modal inputs.

fields.name: mm_processor_cache_type
fields.doc: Type of cache to use for the multi-modal preprocessor/mapper. If `shm`, use shared memory FIFO cache. If `lru`, use mirrored LRU cache.

fields.name: mm_hasher_algorithm
fields.doc: Hash algorithm to use for multi-modal input caching. Use `"sha256"` or `"sha512"` for FIPS-compliant deployments.

fields.name: mm_shm_cache_max_object_size_mb
fields.doc: Size limit (in MiB) for each object stored in the multi-modal processor shared memory cache. Only effective when `mm_processor_cache_type` is `"shm"`.

fields.name: mm_encoder_only
fields.doc: When enabled, skips the language component of the model.

fields.name: mm_encoder_tp_mode
fields.doc: Indicates how to optimize multi-modal encoder inference using tensor parallelism (TP).

fields.name: mm_encoder_attn_backend
fields.doc: Optional override for the multi-modal encoder attention backend when using vision transformers. Accepts any value from `vllm.v1.attention.backends.registry.AttentionBackendEnum` (e.g. `FLASH_ATTN`).

fields.name: mm_encoder_attn_dtype
fields.doc: Optional dtype override for ViT encoder attention. Set to `"fp8"` to enable FP8 quantization via the FlashInfer cuDNN backend. When set to `"fp8"` without a scale file, dynamic scaling is used automatically. See docs/features/quantization/fp8_vit_attn.md for details.

fields.name: mm_encoder_fp8_scale_path
fields.doc: Path to a JSON file containing per-layer FP8 Q/K/V scales for ViT encoder attention. When provided (with `mm_encoder_attn_dtype="fp8"`), static scaling is used. When omitted, dynamic scaling is used.

fields.name: mm_encoder_fp8_scale_save_path
fields.doc: When set with dynamic FP8 scaling (`mm_encoder_attn_dtype="fp8"` and no `mm_encoder_fp8_scale_path`), saves the calibrated scales to this file after the amax history buffer is full. The saved file can then be used as `mm_encoder_fp8_scale_path` in subsequent runs.

fields.name: mm_encoder_fp8_scale_save_margin
fields.doc: Safety margin multiplied onto scales when auto-saving. A value > 1 leaves headroom so that inputs with larger activations than the calibration set do not overflow FP8 range. Default 1.5.

fields.name: interleave_mm_strings
fields.doc: Enable fully interleaved support for multimodal prompts, while using --chat-template-content-format=string.

fields.name: skip_mm_profiling
fields.doc: When enabled, skips multimodal memory profiling and only profiles with language backbone model during engine initialization.

fields.name: video_pruning_rate
fields.doc: Fraction of video tokens to prune from each video. Value sits in range [0;1); pruning is enabled when it is greater than 0. The pruning algorithm is selected by `video_pruning_method`.

fields.name: video_pruning_method
fields.doc: Video token pruning algorithm applied when `video_pruning_rate` > 0: - "evs": Efficient Video Sampling. - "vidcom2": Video Compression Commander.

fields.name: mm_tensor_ipc
fields.doc: IPC (inter-process communication) method for multimodal tensors. - "direct_rpc": Use msgspec serialization via RPC - "torch_shm": Use torch.multiprocessing shared memory for zero-copy IPC Defaults to "direct_rpc".

fields.name: allow_missing_mm_embeddings
fields.doc: Whether a pre-computed-embedding input may omit the `*_embeds` tensor.

fields.name: mm_ipc_gpu_memory_gb
fields.doc: Amount of GPU memory (in GiB) sequestered on the engine's device for GPU-side multimodal work in the API-server (frontend) process, such as hardware video decoding.

classes.name: ObservabilityConfig
classes.doc: Configuration for observability - metrics and tracing.

fields.name: show_hidden_metrics_for_version
fields.doc: Enable deprecated Prometheus metrics that have been hidden since the specified version. For example, if a previously deprecated metric has been hidden since the v0.7.0 release, you use `--show-hidden-metrics-for-version=0.7` as a temporary escape hatch while you migrate to new metrics. The metric is likely to be removed completely in an upcoming release.

fields.name: otlp_traces_endpoint
fields.doc: Target URL to which OpenTelemetry traces will be sent.

fields.name: collect_detailed_traces
fields.doc: It makes sense to set this only if `--otlp-traces-endpoint` is set. If set, it will collect detailed traces for the specified modules. This involves use of possibly costly and or blocking operations and hence might have a performance impact.

fields.name: per_request_spec_decode_metrics
fields.doc: Include per-request speculative-decoding acceptance metrics in the response under `metrics.speculative_decoding`. `none` disables; `summary` adds mean acceptance length, draft acceptance rate, and the step-by-draft-length histogram; `detailed` additionally records the ordered per-step accepted/proposed arrays (one entry per verify step). Only reported for single-sequence requests (`n == 1`), …

fields.name: kv_cache_metrics
fields.doc: Enable KV cache residency metrics (lifetime, idle time, reuse gaps). Uses sampling to minimize overhead. Requires log stats to be enabled (i.e., --disable-log-stats not set).

fields.name: kv_cache_metrics_sample
fields.doc: Sampling rate for KV cache metrics (0.0, 1.0]. Default 0.01 = 1% of blocks.

fields.name: custom_histogram_buckets

fields.name: proton_graph_attribution
fields.doc: Observe CUDA graph capture so replayed kernels can be attributed. Requires Triton >= 3.7 and ``proton_data='tree'``.

fields.doc: If `True`, enables stack tracing in the torch profiler. Enabled by default as it is useful for debugging. Can be disabled via --profiler-config.torch_profiler_with_stack=false CLI flag.

fields.name: torch_profiler_with_flops
fields.doc: If `True`, enables FLOPS counting in the torch profiler. Disabled by default.

fields.name: torch_profiler_use_gzip
fields.doc: If `True`, saves torch profiler traces in gzip format. Enabled by default

fields.name: torch_profiler_dump_cuda_time_total
fields.doc: If `True`, dumps total CUDA time in torch profiler traces. Enabled by default.

fields.name: torch_profiler_record_shapes
fields.doc: If `True`, records tensor shapes in the torch profiler. Disabled by default.

fields.name: torch_profiler_with_memory
fields.doc: If `True`, enables memory profiling in the torch profiler. Disabled by default.

fields.name: capture_torch_profiler
fields.doc: If `True`, enables a torch profiler during CUDA graph capture on rank 0. Traces are saved to a `capture_traces` subdirectory under `torch_profiler_dir`. Requires `profiler` to be set to 'torch'.

fields.name: detailed_trace_annotation
fields.doc: If `True`, uses detailed annotations with roofline metrics (sk, sqsq, sqsk) in profiler trace events. If `False`, uses simple annotations with only context/generation request counts and token counts. Disabled by default.

fields.name: ignore_frontend

fields.name: delay_iterations
fields.doc: Number of engine iterations to skip before starting profiling. Defaults to 0, meaning profiling starts immediately after receiving /start_profile.

fields.name: max_iterations
fields.doc: Maximum number of engine iterations to profile after starting profiling. Defaults to 0, meaning no limit.

fields.name: warmup_iterations

This helps reduce noise from JIT compilation and other one-time costs in the profiled trace. Defaults to 0 (schedule-based profiling disabled, recording all iterations). Set to a positive value (e.g., 2) to enable schedule-based profiling.

fields.name: active_iterations
fields.doc: Number of active iterations for PyTorch profiler schedule. This is the number of iterations where profiling data is actually collected. Defaults to 5 active iterations.

fields.name: wait_iterations
fields.doc: Number of wait iterations for PyTorch profiler schedule. During wait, the profiler is completely off with zero overhead. This allows skipping initial iterations before warmup begins. Defaults to 0 (no wait period).

fields.doc: The scheduler class to use. "vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler.Scheduler" is the default scheduler. Can be a class directly or the path to a class of form "mod.custom_class".

fields.name: disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager
fields.doc: If set to True, KV cache manager will allocate the same size of KV cache for all attention layers even if there are multiple type of attention layers like full attention and sliding window attention. If set to None, the default value will be determined based on the environment and starting configuration.

fields.name: scheduler_reserve_full_isl
fields.doc: If True, the scheduler checks whether the full input sequence length fits in the KV cache before admitting a new request, rather than only checking the first chunk. Prevents over-admission and KV cache thrashing with chunked prefill.

fields.name: watermark
fields.doc: Fraction of total KV cache blocks to keep free (the watermark) when admitting waiting or preempted requests into the running queue. This headroom helps avoid frequent KV cache eviction and the resulting repeated preemption of requests when GPU memory is scarce. Must be in the range [0.0, 1.0); 0.0 (the default) disables the watermark.

fields.name: prefill_schedule_interval
fields.doc: Only admit prefill once every N engine steps, leaving the steps in between to decode alone. 1 (the default) admits prefill on every step.

fields.name: async_scheduling
fields.doc: If set to False, disable async scheduling. Async scheduling helps to avoid gaps in GPU utilization, leading to better latency and throughput.

fields.name: stream_interval
fields.doc: The interval (or buffer size) for streaming in terms of token length. A smaller value (1) makes streaming smoother by sending each token immediately, while a larger value (e.g., 10) reduces host overhead and may increase throughput by batching multiple tokens before sending.

classes.name: SpeculativeConfig
classes.doc: Configuration for speculative decoding.

fields.name: enforce_eager
fields.doc: Override the default enforce_eager from model_config

fields.name: num_speculative_tokens
fields.doc: The number of speculative tokens, if provided. It will default to the number in the draft model config if present, otherwise, it is required.

fields.name: model
fields.doc: The name of the draft model, eagle head, or additional weights, if provided.

fields.name: method
fields.doc: The name of the speculative method to use. If users provide and set the `model` param, the speculative method type will be detected automatically if possible, if `model` param is not provided, the method name must be provided.

fields.name: draft_tensor_parallel_size
fields.doc: The degree of the tensor parallelism for the draft model. Can only be 1 or the same as the target model's tensor parallel size.

fields.name: tensor_parallel_size
fields.doc: Users should pass "draft_tensor_parallel_size". This parameter's purpose is to warn users when they mistakenly provide the wrong argument.

fields.name: quantization
fields.doc: Quantization method that was used to quantize the draft model weights. If `None`, we assume the model weights are not quantized. Note that it only takes effect when using the draft model-based speculative method.

fields.name: moe_backend
fields.doc: MoE backend to use for the draft model. When `None`, the draft model inherits the target model's `--moe-backend` setting. Useful when the drafter and generator require different MoE kernels (e.g. quantized generator with unquantized drafter).

fields.name: attention_backend
fields.doc: Attention backend to use for the draft model. When `None`, the backend is automatically selected. Useful when the drafter requires a different attention backend (e.g. DFlash needs a backend that supports non-causal attention).

fields.name: kv_cache_dtype
fields.doc: KV cache dtype for the draft model. When `None`, the draft inherits the target model's `--kv-cache-dtype`. Custom dtypes registered by platform backends are accepted.

fields.name: max_model_len
fields.doc: The maximum model length of the draft model. Used when testing the ability to skip speculation for some sequences.

fields.name: revision
fields.doc: The specific model version to use for the draft model. It can be a branch name, a tag name, or a commit id. If unspecified, will use the default version.

fields.name: code_revision
fields.doc: The specific revision to use for the draft model code on Hugging Face Hub. It can be a branch name, a tag name, or a commit id. If unspecified, will use the default version.

fields.name: index_share_for_mtp_iteration
fields.doc: Override whether MTP iterations reuse the first step's sparse indices. If `None`, use the value from the draft model's Hugging Face config.

fields.name: disable_padded_drafter_batch
fields.doc: Disable input padding for speculative decoding. If set to True, speculative input batches can contain sequences of different lengths, which may only be supported by certain attention backends. This currently only affects the EAGLE method of speculation.

fields.name: disable_eagle_block_drop
fields.doc: Disable dropping the trailing prefix-cache block for EAGLE-like speculative methods. This is an experimental option for measuring the acceptance-rate impact of reusing that block. It does not disable the speculative drafter itself.

fields.name: draft_lm_head_quantization
fields.doc: Quantize the drafter's copy of a target lm_head it shares (EAGLE and MTP). "fp8" uses per-row weight and per-token activation scales on the platform's FP8 linear kernel; "nvfp4" is weight-only on the platform's W4A16 kernel. The target verifies with its own head, so only the acceptance length can change. Model Runner V2 only.

fields.name: use_local_argmax_reduction
fields.doc: Use vocab-parallel local argmax instead of all-gathering full logits for draft token generation. Reduces communication from O(vocab_size) to O(2 * tp_size) per token. Only applies to greedy draft selection in non-tree speculation.

fields.name: use_heterogeneous_vocab
fields.doc: Allow draft and target models to use different vocabularies. When enabled, builds a token-level intersection at init and constrains draft logits to shared tokens only (TLI algorithm). Requires method='draft_model'.

fields.name: prompt_lookup_max
fields.doc: Maximum size of ngram token window when using Ngram proposer, required when method is set to ngram.

fields.name: prompt_lookup_min
fields.doc: Minimum size of ngram token window when using Ngram proposer, if provided. Defaults to 1.

fields.name: parallel_drafting
fields.doc: Enable parallel drafting, where all speculative tokens are generated in parallel rather than sequentially. This can improve performance but requires the speculative model be trained to support parallel drafting. Only compatible with EAGLE and draft model methods.

fields.name: target_model_config
fields.doc: The configuration of the target model.

fields.name: target_parallel_config
fields.doc: The parallel configuration for the target model.

fields.name: num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size
fields.doc: Batch-size schedule used to dynamically choose speculative-token count.

fields.name: draft_model_config
fields.doc: The configuration of the draft model initialized internal.

fields.name: draft_parallel_config
fields.doc: The parallel configuration for the draft model initialized internal.

fields.name: suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth
fields.doc: The maximum depth of the suffix decoding global and prompt trees. The tree depth limits the sum of the prefix match and speculation lengths.

fields.name: suffix_decoding_max_cached_requests
fields.doc: The maximum number of requests to cache in the global suffix tree. If exceeded, will trigger eviction in FIFO order. If set to 0, the global suffix tree is disabled and past responses are not cached (prompt trees are still used).

fields.name: suffix_decoding_max_spec_factor
fields.doc: The maximum spec factor for suffix decoding. The spec factor controls speculation lengths based on the prefix match length: max_spec_tokens = max_spec_factor * prefix_match_length.

fields.name: suffix_decoding_min_token_prob
fields.doc: The minimum token probability for suffix decoding. Will only speculate tokens with estimated probability (based on frequency counts) greater than or equal to this value.

fields.name: draft_load_config
fields.doc: Load config for the draft model. If not specified, will use the load config from the target model.

fields.name: rejection_sample_method
fields.doc: The rejection sampling method to use. 'standard' uses probabilistic rejection sampling (with or without cached draft logits, controlled by draft_sample_method). 'synthetic' accepts draft tokens with a decaying probability calibrated to synthetic_acceptance_rate. 'block' uses block verification (Sun et al.), which jointly verifies the draft tokens as a block instead of one at a time. 'fly' applies …

fields.name: synthetic_acceptance_rates
fields.doc: Per-position *unconditional* acceptance rates for synthetic rejection sampling. Position i's entry is the marginal probability that the first i+1 draft tokens are all accepted; the list must have length num_speculative_tokens, each entry in [0, 1], and be monotonically non-increasing. Only valid when rejection_sample_method is 'synthetic'. Mutually exclusive with synthetic_acceptance_length.

fields.name: synthetic_acceptance_length
fields.doc: Target mean acceptance length for synthetic rejection sampling, in [1, num_speculative_tokens + 1]. Resolved internally to synthetic_acceptance_rates. Only valid when rejection_sample_method is 'synthetic'. Mutually exclusive with synthetic_acceptance_rates.

fields.name: enable_adaptive_verification
fields.doc: Whether to adaptively size the draft-verification budget from per-request confidence. Currently only supported for method="dspark".

fields.name: draft_sample_method
fields.doc: How the draft model samples tokens. 'greedy' always picks the argmax token, and the draft probabilities are treated as one-hot during rejection sampling. 'probabilistic' samples stochastically from the draft distribution and uses the full draft logits for the probability ratio test during rejection sampling. This comes at the cost of additional GPU memory usage.

fields.name: dspark_draft_topk
fields.doc: For Qwen3 DSpark drafting, evaluate the Markov projection only for the top-k base-logit candidates. Requires draft tensor parallel size 1.

fields.name: fly_window_size
fields.doc: Number of subsequent native acceptance decisions checked by FLy. If unset, defaults to ``min(6, num_speculative_tokens - 1)``.

fields.name: fly_entropy_threshold
fields.doc: Target top-k entropy lower bound for FLy loose acceptance.

fields.name: fly_entropy_top_k
fields.doc: Number of largest target probabilities used by FLy's entropy gate.

classes.name: SpeechToTextConfig
classes.doc: Configuration for speech-to-text models.

fields.name: sample_rate
fields.doc: Sample rate (Hz) to resample input audio to. Most speech models expect 16kHz audio input. The input audio will be automatically resampled to this rate before processing.

fields.name: max_audio_clip_s
fields.doc: Maximum duration in seconds for a single audio clip without chunking. Audio longer than this will be split into smaller chunks if `allow_audio_chunking` evaluates to True, otherwise it will be rejected. `None` means audio duration can be unlimited and won't be chunked.

fields.name: overlap_chunk_second
fields.doc: Overlap duration in seconds between consecutive audio chunks when splitting long audio. This helps maintain context across chunk boundaries and improves transcription quality at split points.

fields.name: min_energy_split_window_size
fields.doc: Window size in samples for finding low-energy (quiet) regions to split audio chunks. The algorithm looks for the quietest moment within this window to minimize cutting through speech. Default 1600 samples ≈ 100ms at 16kHz. If None, no chunking will be done.

classes.name: StructuredOutputsConfig
classes.doc: Dataclass which contains structured outputs config for the engine.

fields.name: backend
fields.doc: Which engine will be used for structured outputs (e.g. JSON schema, regex, etc) by default. With "auto", we will make opinionated choices based on request contents and what the backend libraries currently support, so the behavior is subject to change in each release.

fields.name: disable_any_whitespace
fields.doc: If `True`, json output will always be compact without any whitespace. If `False`, the model may generate whitespace between JSON fields, which is still valid JSON. This is only supported for xgrammar and guidance backends.

fields.name: disable_additional_properties
fields.doc: If `True`, the `guidance` backend will not use `additionalProperties` in the JSON schema. This is only supported for the `guidance` backend and is used to better align its behaviour with `outlines` and `xgrammar`.

fields.name: reasoning_parser
fields.doc: Select the reasoning parser depending on the model that you're using. This is used to parse the reasoning content into OpenAI API format.

fields.name: reasoning_parser_plugin
fields.doc: Path to a dynamically reasoning parser plugin that can be dynamically loaded and registered.

fields.name: enable_in_reasoning
fields.doc: Whether to use structured input for reasoning.

fields.name: aux_output_config

fields.name: engram_config
fields.doc: N-gram embedding storage and sharding settings.

fields.name: mamba_config
fields.doc: Mamba configuration.

fields.doc: Kernel configuration.

fields.name: profiler_config

fields.name: kv_events_config
fields.doc: The configurations for event publishing.

fields.name: ec_transfer_config
fields.doc: The configurations for distributed EC cache transfer.

fields.name: ec_manager_config
fields.doc: The configurations for custom encoder cache manager.

fields.name: reasoning_config
fields.doc: The configurations for reasoning model.

fields.name: additional_config
fields.doc: Additional config for specified platform. Different platforms may support different configs. Make sure the configs are valid for the platform you are using. Contents must be hashable.

fields.name: instance_id
fields.doc: The ID of the vLLM instance.

fields.name: optimization_level
fields.doc: The optimization level. These levels trade startup time cost for performance, with -O0 having the best startup time and -O3 having the best performance. -O2 is used by default. See OptimizationLevel for full description.

fields.name: performance_mode
fields.doc: Performance mode for runtime behavior, 'balanced' is the default. 'interactivity' favors low end-to-end per-request latency at small batch sizes (fine-grained CUDA graphs, latency-oriented kernels). 'throughput' favors aggregate tokens/sec at high concurrency (larger CUDA graphs, more aggressive batching, throughput-oriented kernels).

fields.name: weight_transfer_config
fields.doc: The configurations for weight transfer during RL training.

fields.name: watchdog_config
fields.doc: Configuration for the stack-dump watchdog.

fields.name: shutdown_timeout
fields.doc: Shutdown grace period for in-flight requests. Shutdown will be delayed for up to this amount of time to allow already-running requests to complete. Any remaining requests are aborted once the timeout is reached.

classes.name: WatchdogConfig
classes.doc: Configuration for the stack-dump watchdog.

fields.name: timeout
fields.doc: Timeout in seconds after which the watchdog considers the process to be stuck and dumps stack traces. Must be greater than 0.

fields.name: check_interval
fields.doc: Interval in seconds at which the watchdog checks for feed timeouts.

fields.name: dump_dir
fields.doc: Directory to save stack dump files. Empty string disables the watchdog feature.

classes.name: WatermarkConfig
classes.doc: Configuration for text watermark generation.

fields.name: key
fields.doc: Secret key used to watermark generated text.

fields.name: algorithm
fields.doc: Algorithm used to watermark generated text.

fields.name: alpha
fields.doc: Probability of selecting key B for dual-key watermarking.

fields.name: context_width
fields.doc: Number of prior tokens used by the watermark PRF.

fields.name: deduplicate_contexts
fields.doc: Which history is searched for a repeated context before a token is sampled; a repeated context is sampled without the watermark. `none` disables the search. `single_turn` (default) searches this request's generated tokens. `all` also searches the prompt and samples the first `context_width` generated tokens without watermarking.

fields.name: deduplicate_contexts_max_history
fields.doc: Number of most recent history positions searched (default 8192), or `None` for the whole scope. Each position is compared over the `context_width` tokens before it. Ignored when `deduplicate_contexts` is `none`.

fields.name: prf
fields.doc: Pseudorandom function used by the watermarking algorithm.

fields.name: allow_target_only_watermarking
fields.doc: Allow speculative decoding without watermarking draft tokens.
